method: Read every unique English-source string group in every file and compare meaning, script, modal strength and technical context. Checked remaining repeated leaves by source-group equality and validated every full file with exported validateTranslation. This is model review, not a native-speaker certification.

files.notes: Traditional Chinese throughout; Taiwan-oriented terminology is coherent. All key distinctions are explicit, including expected maintenance recovery and excessive requests.
Hong Kong written Chinese, not colloquial Cantonese. Traditional characters and regional lexical choices are coherent; no semantic omission identified.
Sorani/Central Kurdish in Arabic script. Source-server, timeout, abnormal versus malicious traffic and domain/IP association are preserved. Technical and idiomatic review confidence is limited.
Dari/Afghan Persian wording is coherent, including مصروف, کوشش and پروتوکول. Does not merely relabel an unrelated language. Important modal/conditional differences are preserved.
Tok Pisin clause structure and loans are recognizable and distinct from Bislama. Plain-language explanations preserve technical meaning. Specialist terminology/register remains a review limitation.
Bislama clause structure is distinct from Tok Pisin. HTTP/HTTPS attempt, unusual connections and expected recovery are preserved; technical loan choices remain review-sensitive.
Tetum grammar and Portuguese-derived technical vocabulary are coherent. Possible causes, timeout and temporary origin unavailability are preserved; local technical register remains lower confidence.
Waray wording and function words are consistent. Flooding explicitly means excessive requests. Some register/spelling choices may merit local refinement, but no necessary semantic correction found.

Sanskrit in Devanagari with retained technical identifiers. Corrected two causative imperatives. Modern computing loans and stylistic choices remain review-sensitive; future passive wording was retained after checking grammar.
Māori orthography and core clauses are coherent. Technical compounds/circumlocutions merit specialist review; no concrete meaning loss identified.
Samoan wording preserves the error distinctions. ASCII apostrophe use is consistent with common keyboard text; not a script problem. Technical loan conventions remain review-sensitive.
Standard Fijian, not Fiji Hindi. Clause meaning and source-server explanation are consistent; technical register remains lower confidence.

Tongan with ʻ punctuation, macrons and definitive accents; technical English loans remain identifiers or local computing terms. No concrete semantic omission identified; regional idiom remains lower confidence.
